title: Halcyon FX weeks 8–9: small demo sample, a rule bug found and fixed, figures unverified
author: Teh_Eno
selftext:
Disclosure: I built this EA and sell it.

Halcyon has been about a year in development, with many iterations. It first ran on a live account in mid-Sep 2026, and that live run ended in late October. Right now it only runs on two demo accounts. One uses AI: a local bridge asks Claude to confirm or veto each entry, and Claude can only block trades, never create them. The other runs the same EA with no AI.

**Please read this first:** the numbers below come from the EA's own trade logs as gross R, which means before spread and costs. I haven't reconciled them with the broker statement yet, so treat them as unverified. There are no cash figures, % return, profit factor or drawdown this time.

**Week of 2–8 Nov:** I don't have reconciled figures for this week, so I'm not reporting any. That doesn't mean it was flat.

**Week of 9–15 Nov (Sydney time), from the logs:**

AI demo:

* 3 entries
* 2 closed, both winners, about +2.5R gross
* 1 still open at the time I checked

No-AI demo:

* 5 entries
* 2 closed, one at +0.5R and one at −1.0R, about −0.5R gross
* 3 still open at the time I checked

**A bug I found:** Halcyon has a hard rule that it never buys into a supply zone and never sells into a demand zone. On the previous build, one setting skipped the higher-timeframe zone check in some cases. That let 3 GBPCAD buys fill inside a daily supply zone and one NZDJPY sell fill inside a daily demand zone. Some of this week's trades came from that flaw, so don't read anything into them.

On Sunday 15 Nov I loaded a new build on both demos that removes that exception. The block now applies on H1, H4 and D1 with no bypass, and the AI can't override it. In backtesting from 1 Sep to 13 Nov it made no wrong-side fills. It has only been running on the demos for a day, though, so I'll report it separately once it has some trades behind it.

With only a handful of trades a week, one week can swing the results a lot either way, so this says very little on its own. I'll keep posting the rough weeks along with the good ones.

Not financial advice. Trading forex is risky, past results don't guarantee future ones, and you can lose money.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: the bypass is the more useful finding than the veto numbers I asked about last time. one check before trusting the fix: replay the OLD build over 1 Sep to 13 Nov too. if that backtest also shows zero wrong-side fills, the backtest can't see the bug, and the new build's clean run proves nothing yet.
